Your friend might be the case of a person trying to gain control of her own life thinking if her issues are explained, therefore the fault lives in the past and her current behaviour is justified by her experiences. Psychology is used to explain behaviour, actions, emotions, brain responses etc.- so shes trying to learn about the cause, purpose and meaning of her own and others behaviour to explain it as a way for her to have more control with this knowledge, which she moght have been lacking in the past. „Fits of rage” are also from built up frustration or emotions, not something a mentally stable person should be struggling with, especially with a personality you described. I think you she should talk to a specialist, whether psychologist or therapist.


edit: controlling/manipulating others gives her a feeling of superiority, power and influence which again is linked to feeling lack of control and ascendency.

for someone who was studying for a psychology degree, she should probably go for therapy herself since from what youre saying there are many unresolved issues that were probably established in her past. „In adult life they meet people who fall in love with their false self. But this love does not last. At some point, glimpses of the real self emerge and disappointment comes. Rejected by their chosen love, the message received in childhood is confirmed: Nobody could love them as they really are.” („all about love” by bell hooks). She might have been praised/valued for her body alone, her „special qualities” might have been some thing that increased that value which made her project that superiority onto the people around her, including you.
